sentences.text:
R Musalaiah Naidu vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 16 May,
2024
 In The High Court Of Andhra Pradesh :: Amaravati
 The Honourable Sri Justice Subba Reddy Satti
 Writ Petition No.11777 Of 2024
Between:
R.Musalaiah Naidu, S/o.R.Venkatappa Naidu,
R/o.Door No.1-10, Jambulapadu, Tadipatri Mandal,
Ananthapuram District, Andhra Pradesh.

entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh :: Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
AND The Government of Andhra Pradesh,
Rep. by its Principal Secretary, Revenue Department,
Secretariat Buildings, Amaravati, and others

... Respondents Counsel for the petitioner : Mr.P.Ravikanth Counsel for respondents 1 to 4 : The G.P. for Land Acquisition Counsel for the 5th respondent : Mr.S.S.Varma, Standing Counsel Counsel for respondents 6 & 7 : Mr.M.Gnaneswara Rao ORDER:
Heard Mr.S.Ramalakshman Reddy, learned counsel representing Mr.P.Ravikanth, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Also heard Smt.T.Lakshmi Padmaja, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the respondent Nos.1 to 4, Mr.Ch.Viswanath, learned counsel representing Mr.S.S.Varma, learned Standing Counsel for the 5th respondent/National Highways Authority of India and Mr.M.Gnaneswara Rao, learned counsel for the respondent Nos.6 and 7.
2.

The writ petition is filed seeking to declare the action of the respondents in trying to dispossess the petitioner from House No.1/1, bearing Assessment No.318/c along with open property admeasuring Acs.1.25 cents situated in Survey No.318-C of Hussainapuram Village, Near Arjas Steel Plant, Tadipatri Mandal, Ananthapuram District, in the guise of land acquisition for National Highway expansion as illegal and arbitrary.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the Notification under Section 3A of the National Highways Act, 1956 (for short, the NH Act) was published in Andhra Jyothi Newspaper on 26.7.2022, but thereafter no proceedings took place.
He would submit that without following the due process of law, the Authorities are trying to interfere with the subject matter property.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition, on written instructions, would submit that in respect Ac.0.75 cents in Survey No.318-C1 Notification was published under Section 3A of the NH Act vide LR.No:LA3(A)/TO/NH-67/ 2022-23, dated 23.7.2022 and after following the procedure Award No.04/2023 was passed on 19.5.2023.

She would submit that the Land Acquisition Officer determined the compensation at Rs.15,00,000/- (Rupees fifteen lakhs only) for the notified extent of Ac.0.75 cents in Survey No.318-C1, however, the compensation was not paid to the petitioner since the title is not confirmed.
5.
In reply, the learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that in view of the subsequent developments, liberty may be granted to the petitioner to take appropriate steps.
Given the said submission, no further orders are required in this writ petition.
6. Accordingly, the writ petition is closed, granting liberty as prayed for.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.

SUBBA REDDY SATTI, J May 16, 2024 vasu R Musalaiah Naidu vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118254959/
